rationale: Evidence from the iteration 5 race (kp 3.5, kd 0.8, base_speed 1.0, ki 0, iteration 0 sensor layout) scored 561.9, below the best raced design (iteration 4, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, 600.5). The oval still finished 20 of 20 with progress 0.9995 and line-loss events of 0.85. Slalom progress rose from 0.215 to 0.276, the first clear movement on the weakest track, but it still has 0 of 20 completions and max_error 0.0628. The s-bend fell from 14 of 20 finishes to 10 of 20 (progress 0.875, down from 0.958), and that drop caused the lower score. Steering oscillation did not rise: the s-bend fell to 0.373 and the oval held at 0.26. The race therefore shows that kp moves slalom progress, but at kp 3.5 it costs s-bend completions. Under the Evaluator's rule, the oval still at 20 of 20 means kp is the slalom lever, so the next test is kp 3.8 with every other value held at the iteration 5 settings. This isolates kp again. Expected result, which is a hypothesis and not a measured outcome: slalom progress rises above 0.30 with the oval still at 20 of 20, while s-bend completions may fall further. Main risk: the s-bend losses at kp 3.5 suggest a trade-off, so if s-bend completions drop below 10 and slalom stays flat, I would return to kp 3.0 and test ki 0.05 to 0.1 next. The sensor layout and weights stay fixed, since widening the array in iteration 1 did not help and the sensor-limit hypothesis is not yet tested. Measurements requested: all eight, on all three tracks, so the kp effect on slalom and on s-bend can be separated.
